newsitem.title: FRANCE: French train conductors to vote on ending strike.
newsitem.headline: French train conductors to vote on ending strike.

text.p: Striking French train conductors were due to vote on Friday on whether to end a three-day stoppage after union leaders made progress in marathon talks with management on pay and conditions.
"We obtained significant advances," said Bruno Dalberto, head of the pro-Socialist CFDT rail union after overnight talks ended at about 5 a.m. (0300 GMT).

Conductors planned to hold meetings around the country on Friday morning and vote on offers, ranging from higher bonuses to a plan to hire more staff. The strike has cut services by about a third on high-speed TGV and regional lines across France.
High-speed trains between Paris and Brussels and Eurostar trains connecting London to Paris and Brussels through the Channel tunnel have been unaffected by the strike.

Even if strikers agree to return to work, traffic would take several hours to return to normal, threatening misery for travellers leaving for a long Pentecost weekend. Trains cannot run without conductors, who are responsible for safety as well as checking tickets.
The conductors staged a similar strike last month, a new sign of opposition to austerity policies by the centre-right government of Prime Minister Alain Juppe.

SNCF management had said it was willing to pursue negotiations opened several weeks ago, but it could not improve its terms because of financial constraints and the need to preserve fairness among the company's staff.
